name: Prize crossword No 29,506
preamble: A dozen of a kind are missing from their clues’ wordplay.

clue.text: Threaten to take on Boatman: it’s hard work

indicators.note: to take something on is to accept it into yourself, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to lour is to look threatening, as a dark sky does
the setter's pseudonym read as a sailor: an AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: The setter jokes that taking him on is a menacing, exhausting business.
explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is the setter's own name, but here it plays a boatman in the ordinary sense, a sailor, AB. This clue has no missing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour is a plain synonym for toil or strenuous physical effort.

clue.text: When they say life begins: key to their confusion

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase standing for the fortieth birthday

indicators.note: letters thrown into confusion lose their order and must be sorted out afresh

blocks.note: F is a musical key
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wry nod to the saying that life begins at forty, and the muddle people feel on reaching it.
explanation.walkthrough: The key is part of the letters being mixed, not a separate add-on. No animal is missing here.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says life begins at forty, so the birthday it points to is the fortieth one.

clue.text: Some pay dividends on board

indicators.note: something on board a ship sits between the letters that stand for a steamship

blocks.note: SS is steamship; on board means inside its two letters
nothing in the clue: the hare is one of the twelve animals the preamble says are missing from the wordplay

explanation.surface: Some stocks pay dividends to those who sit on the company board.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says twelve animals are missing from the wordplay; here the missing hare goes aboard the steamship SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Company shares are units of ownership, and many of them earn their holders regular dividend payments.

clue.text: Return to city of legend

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: nothing in the clue: the camel is one of the twelve animals the preamble says are missing from the wordplay
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: An invitation to go back to a fabled city.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the little word to is turned round; the missing camel stands in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelot is King Arthur's court in the Arthurian romances, a legendary place rather than a real one.

clue.text: Conquest of the heavens

blocks.note: a conquest is a win
nothing in the clue: the elk is one of the twelve animals the preamble says are missing from the wordplay

explanation.surface: It sounds like a space race: conquering the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: With the animal gone, the instruction to put it inside goes too, so the solver supplies both the elk and its place inside the win.
explanation.definitionFit: Welkin is an old poetic word for the sky or the vault of heaven, as in 'make the welkin ring'.

clue.text: Prompt service assistant

blocks.note: a cue is a prompt, as given to an actor
nothing in the clue: the rat is one of the twelve animals the preamble says are missing from the wordplay

explanation.surface: It reads like a request for quick, efficient help at a counter.
explanation.walkthrough: Prompt looks like an adjective meaning quick, but it is the noun, a cue; the missing rat sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is a junior cleric who helps the vicar or rector, including in leading church services.

clue.text: Biographical novel with no big characters and limited in scope

indicators.note: something novel is new, so these letters take a new form
to be with no thing is to lack it, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
the characters, or letters, of the word big, which are removed

explanation.surface: A book reviewer dismisses a life story with no major figures as narrow.
explanation.walkthrough: Big characters look like important people in the story; they are just the three letters B, I, G, taken out before the rest is rearranged. No animal is missing here.
explanation.definitionFit: Parochial means having a narrow, local outlook, like someone whose interests stop at the parish boundary.

clue.text: The cards show Boatman joining Murdoch title? On the contrary

indicators.note: one thing joining another is placed next to it in a line
the contrary of a thing is its opposite, so the newspaper name runs the opposite way

blocks.note: the setter refers to himself, so his name gives ME
The Sun is a British tabloid owned by Rupert Murdoch's company

explanation.surface: Tarot cards foretelling the setter writing for a Murdoch paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The cards wants to mean playing cards or a fortune-teller's deck, but it means the cards a restaurant hands you. No animal is missing here.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is often a printed card listing the dishes, so diners may ask for the cards.

clue.text: Dishes from where dishes come from

blocks.note: pies are baked dishes
nothing in the clue: the otter is one of the twelve animals the preamble says are missing from the wordplay

explanation.surface: A riddle about where crockery is made.
explanation.walkthrough: The two uses of dishes are different: food in the wordplay, crockery in the definition. The Potteries is the area around Stoke-on-Trent in England, famous for china and ceramics.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potteries is the English district that has long made much of Britain's tableware, plates and bowls.

clue.text: Snake undergoing surgery by knife

indicators.note: something undergoing surgery is cut open and rearranged on the table

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A snake on the operating table, under the surgeon's knife.
explanation.walkthrough: The snake is not one of the missing animals: it is printed in the clue and its letters are simply mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A skean, or sgian-dubh, is a small Scottish dagger traditionally tucked into the sock with Highland dress.

clue.text: From a place in Africa, cycling to a place in South America

indicators.note: a cycle goes round and round, so letters from the front come round to the back

blocks.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A bike ride from one continent to another.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two letters move to the end. No animal is missing here.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital city of Peru, on the Pacific coast of South America.

clue.text: Types books?

blocks.note: first meaning: kinds or classes
second meaning: reserves or requests goods, as when you book a meal

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like nouns from printing or publishing, but books is a verb here. No animal is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Order means a class or kind, and to order something is to reserve or request it.

clue.text: Determined position of editor: wrong about nurse

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of place and need setting right
to be about something is to be all around it

blocks.note: taken as written
EN is Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade

explanation.surface: An editor is set on a position, but has got it wrong about a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: Editor wants to be ED, but all six letters are mixed and wrapped round the nurse. No animal is missing here.
explanation.definitionFit: To orient something is to find or fix its position relative to the compass or surroundings.

clue.text: See 17
Country house, somewhat dilapidated, at Chatham

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only some of the following letters count

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An estate agent's description of a run-down property in Chatham, a town in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma is ignored. No animal is missing here.
explanation.definitionFit: A datcha, more often spelt dacha, is a Russian holiday cottage or villa in the countryside.

clue.text: Familiar textile designer reportedly was obliged to pay source of charged material

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the spoken form counts

blocks.note: Cath Kidston, a British designer of floral prints, called by her first name as a friend would
someone obliged to pay owed the money

explanation.surface: A designer's debt to a fabric supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: Familiar signals a first name, not a well-known person. No animal is missing here.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathode is the electrode that gives off electrons, the negatively charged particles, in a valve or cell.

clue.text: See 15
A1 vessel? Mine capsized

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, and in a down entry that turns the letters round

blocks.note: a pot is a vessel for holding things
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A first-class ship that was holed by a mine and turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: Vessel and capsized suggest a ship, but the vessel is a pot. A1 is a top rating, from the shipping register Lloyd's. No animal is missing here.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptop and A1 are both informal ways of saying first-rate or excellent.

clue.text: End of empire for former head of state

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter alone

blocks.note: nothing in the clue: the dog is one of the twelve animals the preamble says are missing from the wordplay
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A deposed ruler watches the end of his empire.
explanation.walkthrough: The missing dog comes first, then the last letter of empire.
explanation.definitionFit: The doge was the elected ruler of the old republics of Venice and Genoa, an office long abolished.

clue.text: Section of low wall

blocks.note: a section is a part
nothing in the clue: the ape is one of the twelve animals the preamble says are missing from the wordplay

explanation.surface: Part of a wall that isn't very high.
explanation.walkthrough: Section of looks like it wants a hidden word, but the missing ape goes inside a part.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall along the edge of a roof, bridge or balcony.

clue.text: Liable to get reaction from each and every other merry grinch

indicators.note: other here means alternate, so one letter is kept and the next skipped throughout

blocks.note: each and every one is all of them
the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Every merry-making killjoy provokes a reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: Every other belongs to the letter selection, not to each and every; the Grinch is the Dr Seuss character who hates Christmas. No animal is missing here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone allergic has a bodily sensitivity that makes them prone to react badly to some substance.

clue.text: Work together to create script for ceremony

blocks.note: nothing in the clue: the cow is one of the twelve animals the preamble says are missing from the wordplay
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: Two people collaborate on the words for a wedding or service.
explanation.walkthrough: Script and ceremony seem to belong together, but the definition ends at script; the missing cow comes before the rite.
explanation.definitionFit: To co-write is to share authorship of a text, so it means collaborating on a piece of writing.

clue.text: Notes sequence of moves in opera about horse, opening in Italy

indicators.note: when a group moves in, its members are shuffled about from where they stood
an opening is a beginning, so only the first letter is wanted
to be about something is to be all around it

blocks.note: taken as written
gee-gee is a childish word for a horse
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Stage directions for an Italian opera in which a horse appears.
explanation.walkthrough: The horse is printed in the clue, so it is not one of the missing animals; the rearranged opera wraps round it and the I.
explanation.definitionFit: An arpeggio is a chord whose notes are played one after another rather than together.

clue.text: You are upset over climbing rose?

definitions.note: a pronoun standing for the person reading this clue

indicators.note: things that are upset are knocked about and end up out of order
something climbing in a down entry goes upwards, so its letters run bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
rose is a pinkish-red colour

explanation.surface: Someone is upset about a rambling rose in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Over places the first piece above the second in a down entry. Climbing rose suggests a plant, but rose is a colour. No animal is missing here.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter addresses the solver as you, and the solver is the reader of the clue, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Election: Colombo regime all losing heart again

indicators.note: every word loses its middle, leaving only its first and last letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters
the first and last letters
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A news report on a Sri Lankan election in which the government loses heart. Colombo is the main city of Sri Lanka.
explanation.walkthrough: All means each of the three words is gutted separately. No animal is missing here.
explanation.definitionFit: Encore is the French word audiences shout when they want a performer to do it once more.

clue.text: Use calf, ham: emit skinless sausage

the letters left when the first and last are removed
the letters left when the first and last are removed
the letters left when the first and last are removed

explanation.surface: A butcher's recipe: veal and ham made into a sausage without casing.
explanation.walkthrough: Skinless sausage suggests a kind of banger, but skinless applies to each of the four words before it. No animal is missing here.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, highly seasoned Italian sausage usually eaten sliced and cold.

clue.text: One drinks too much from tap

blocks.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
nothing in the clue: the pig is one of the twelve animals the preamble says are missing from the wordplay

explanation.surface: A drinker helping himself straight from the barrel tap.
explanation.walkthrough: The missing pig sits inside the drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a small peg or tap used to draw liquid from a cask or barrel.

clue.text: The antithesis of a son of a gun

blocks.note: a mam, a dialect word for a mother, is the female parent, the opposite of a male child
nothing in the clue: the gnu is one of the twelve animals the preamble says are missing from the wordplay

explanation.surface: It plays on 'son of a gun', a mild oath, asking what the opposite would be.
explanation.walkthrough: Son of a gun reads as a set phrase, but it splits after son. Mam is used in northern England, Wales and Ireland for mum; the missing gnu goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnum is a type of powerful handgun cartridge and the revolver that fires it, as in the .357 Magnum.

clue.text: Unforeseen problem for church

blocks.note: nothing in the clue: the cat is one of the twelve animals the preamble says are missing from the wordplay
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A parish faces an unexpected difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: With the cat missing, only church is left as wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch is a hidden snag or drawback that turns up only once you look closely.

clue.text: Profits from imperfect markets are about: boast about it

definitions.note: a plural noun phrase for a mass noun naming the practice

indicators.note: to be about something is to be all around it, and the word does that job twice

blocks.note: taken as written
to brag is to boast
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trader brags about profits made from market inefficiencies.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: it goes inside brag after the B, and that goes inside are after the R. No animal is missing here.
explanation.definitionFit: Arbitrage is buying and selling the same asset in different markets to profit from a price difference.

clue.text: Daughter of Vandyke, perhaps

blocks.note: nothing in the clue: the bear is one of the twelve animals the preamble says are missing from the wordplay

explanation.surface: It asks about a child of the painter Anthony van Dyck.
explanation.walkthrough: Vandyke looks like the painter, but here it is the style named after his portraits; the missing bear comes before the D.
explanation.definitionFit: A Vandyke is a neat pointed chin beard, often with a moustache, as worn by sitters in van Dyck's portraits.

clue.text: Riotous Assembly follows a constable’s initial induction: it’s shocking

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so this part is placed second
an assembly puts parts together into a new structure
an initial is the first letter of a word
induction is bringing something in, so one piece is put inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A literary note on Riotous Assembly, Tom Sharpe's farce about South African policemen, whose bungling constable makes it shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: Riotous Assembly reads as the novel's title, but riotous is the letters and assembly the instruction to rearrange them. No animal is missing here.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrocious and shocking both describe something appallingly bad or wicked enough to horrify people.
